Negative Appraisals.value: I have lost my faith in people, life, or a higher power
I feel that others can see what happened to me just by looking at me

vignette: Mohammed, a 41-year-old Middle Eastern man married and working as a dancer, has been struggling with the aftermath of his experiences in a war-torn country. The trauma he experienced there has profoundly affected his life since his return to America. During the time he spent in the war zone, Mohammed witnessed the destruction of his home city and the loss of several close friends. One particularly harrowing day, while walking near a field that had been bombed, he heard sudden, shattering explosions followed by the pungent smell of burning earth and smoke. This auditory assault, coupled with the acrid scent of soil and outdoor debris, left an indelible mark on him. Since returning to his life in America, Mohammed has found himself frequently triggered by sounds reminiscent of those explosions and the smells of damp soil or outdoor environments. These triggers are not mere annoyances; they transport him back to that moment with vivid clarity, reigniting feelings of fear and helplessness he experienced during the bombing. His marriage has also been affected by these triggers. His wife often comments on how quiet he becomes when she mentions names related to his time in the war zone, or when they walk near a park after it rains. Mohammed finds himself withdrawing into a shell, feeling dead inside as if he’s lost touch with his emotions and sense of self. What frightens Mohammed most is not just these triggers themselves but what they represent about his internal state. He has come to believe that others can see the horror he experienced merely by looking at him. This belief exacerbates his feelings of emotional numbness, making it difficult for him to engage fully with people around him or even to perform on stage as a dancer. His performance is now marred by an underlying current of unease and anxiety. Mohammed’s faith in life and humanity has been shaken to its core. He feels he has lost his sense of purpose and connection to the world, finding it hard to trust others or feel hopeful about the future. These negative appraisals have become a self-reinforcing cycle; every time he is triggered by a sound or smell, these feelings intensify, making him more likely to withdraw further into himself. It was during one of his dance rehearsals that Mohammed finally decided to seek help. The combination of hearing a firecracker go off outside the studio and catching a whiff of earth from someone who had just stepped inside caused an intense flashback. He froze in place, unable to continue dancing or even respond when asked if he was okay. This episode marked a turning point for Mohammed. While he fears that his past experiences will always haunt him, he is hopeful that with the right support and guidance, he can regain some semblance of the life he once had—a life where he feels alive again and not just a shell of himself. He hopes to find ways to manage his triggers more effectively so that they do not continue to erode his sense of self and connection to those around him.
